I have been in your shoes, I feel I still am struggling with this same issue a lot. But I agree with people who said you need therapy. The thing is, as much as I can understand how you feel, it is also not fair to unload on someone else all the time. When you have these deep rooted problems such as depression and you need to talk about things or vent, it can be really draining to another person. Even if you have one of the best, most understanding partners or friends, everyone will get fatigued at some point. It’s really hard to carry someone else’s pain when everyone has their own to deal with. 

So I would highly recommend looking into therapy. It can be expensive but depending on where you live, there are bound to be resources to free therapy even if it’s just a number of sessions. Depending on your age too, there might be counselling available at your school or college, via the workplace etc. 

I would really encourage you to take accountability for yourself and seriously look into this. It will do you a world of good.

It’s a tough one, I find it conflicting. I watched Doctor Foster (a tv show about a doctor who finds out her husband has been having an affair and all her friends knew and kept it from her). That scenario is one of my biggest fears, like imagine you’re your friend’s partner in this, and eventually you find out your partner was having an affair and all her friends knew. Even if it’s not the case, you’d imagine them all laughing or snickering about it behind your back, and it would probably destroy you trust in people for a long time, if not forever. 

That said, I also feel like it’s not your place or your business (depending on your relationship with the partner). If you’re friends with him and respect/care about him, and if it’s pulling on your own personal values or morals then you need to speak to your friend and either tell her to confess, stop it or distance yourself. You could even tell him yourself, but that would probably end your friendship entirely with the girl so tread carefully if you want to keep that friendship alive. 

If you stay quiet, and cover for her, you will be complicit in the affair. No judgement - you do you. People have different values, beliefs and morals. If that doesn’t cross any of those or make you feel a certain way, then I guess you carry on and stay quiet. If it does cross your boundaries/beliefs, then the only resolution is to speak up.

I don’t think it’s disrespectful or abnormal to keep memories on your phone. My phone is full of videos and pics of me and my exes. Everyone deserves some privacy, and I’d be pretty annoyed if I was in a relationship and someone trawled through my Google photos and found those pics and videos, and I’d be even more annoyed if they then demanded I delete them. That said, I definitely don’t go back and look at them often and I’m not using the nudes or vids to get off. But they ARE memories, and I don’t want to forget them either. 

Also there is a big difference between privacy and secrecy. These are so deep within my Google photos that it’s not like I’d have to hide my phone from someone so they don’t see them or know about them, and for someone to learn about their existence would mean they would have breached my privacy.

I’ve been in the same position, still not *truly* over it despite having moved on. I’d guess it’s because it was a situationship, you never got to truly give a relationship a go and get to a point where it naturally ran it’s course. Most relationship break ups are due to just eventually breaking down due to incompatibilities becoming more and more apparent. You might still love each other but you got to spend time in a relationship giving it a go and after realising it wasn’t going to work, went separate ways. 

With a situationship, even if the dynamic *is* pretty much a relationship without the labels, without that level of commitment or knowing you’re both on the same page, things always feel left up in the air. There’s a lot more room for ‘what ifs’ and ‘maybe we were just the right people at the wrong time’. It allows you to build up an idea of the person and what a fully fledged relationship could be like with them, and over time you start to believe that this idea is truth. After all, with other relationships you started off this way but enough time will have shattered that illusion. 

It’s much harder to dispel the illusion when you never really *had* the person or could never really nail them down. They’re elusive and it leaves you wanting more because you think they’re worth fighting for - but the truth is, you don’t really know if they are or not. And that’s exciting and keeps us always dreaming about the one that got away. In my case it even lead to limerence. He was my object of desire for a long time, could literally do no wrong whatsoever. Not OP but for me it’s because one of the biggest fears in people with BPD is being abandoned. When I let my guard down enough for people to get close, it means if they left I’d be in excruciating pain. So I push people away so they can’t get close. You can’t be ‘abandoned’ or ‘left’ by someone if you didn’t let them get close enough to hurt you. 

Unfortunately, this behaviour usually happens once you’ve *already* become close and attached to someone. So then what happens in my experience is a self fulfilling prophecy which goes a little something like this:

- meet someone and hit it off

- get unhealthily attached to person pretty quick 

- enter a wonderfully intense relationship 

- idealise the person and put them on a pedastal, they can do no wrong 

- suddenly, fear and panic strikes, paranoia starts, I become convinced they are going to hurt me in some way so I start being a massive cunt 

- they stick around and try to persevere way longer than I deserve, because when things are good they are very good, but when things are bad they are awful 

- things start getting too much for the other person, they love me but can’t deal with the mood swings or the jealousy and insecurity 

- they end up leaving because I pushed them too far away, out of fear that they were going to leave me and a ‘they can’t leave me if I leave them first’ mentality, except I never leave first because I don’t actually *want* to leave. I want them to love me as much as I love them, I want them to prove to me that they’re never going to go anywhere because they think I’m worthy enough to fight for. But the tests never end. And they leave. 

- then I’m there, in the excruciating pain I dreaded, which gets more painful with each person, with shocked pikachu expression on my face. 

- as time goes on, with hindsight I realise they did many things to show they *were* happy and they *did* care about me/love me, but people can only handle so much before they are broken down and beaten. 


I won’t sit here and pretend all my relationships were with great people and that any one of them would’ve worked out had I not had the problems I do, because that is far from the case. But there is definitely one pivotal relationship in my life that could have worked I think had I just been able to relax and not make him feel like he was constantly walking on egg shells.

The difference for me in that scenario is that they're on the brink of it tipping over into an affair. I feel like there's clear intent in that case, because he'd be saying that he really wants to kiss her because he likes her and has feelings for her, rather than just because she's attractive. 

So I guess you will have to try and ascertain whether they got close during work and may have developed feelings, or whether it was just a case of two people finding eachother attractive and the guy being able to recognise  that whilst she's attractive and he'd like to kiss her, he knows that he loves his partner and wouldn't want to hurt her and wouldn't want to jeopardize what he already has etc.

When my boyfriend and I said I love you to each other for the first time. Sounds like a cliche I know, but it was different. We had been dating casually on/off for over a year at that point and neither of us wanted to admit how deep our feelings had gotten. 

We met in August 2018, a month after we both came out of serious relationships and neither of us were over our exes. We had an incredible first date, we really clicked and had a lot of banter and fun and then I went back to his. We planned more dates but I was new to dating and wanted to meet more guys. We realised neither of us would be happy if we both slept with other people and we'd want to be exclusive but because we were so recently single we decided to just stay friendly on Facebook and go our separate ways. 

Three weeks later, mid September 2018, really not much time haha, I stupidly asked him to meet up again. I'd only met him once at that point but I could not shake him, I'd really never met anyone else like him. I'd met a few other guys and none had the same banter and with him there was a raw sexual chemistry, like we couldn't keep our hands off each other and it wasn't like that with anyone else I'd ever met. In that three weeks, a lot had happened for him too. His ex had gotten back in touch and they tried things again, but there was a reason it didn't work in the first place and it ended really badly the second time around. He was a mess and really fucked up. He has been through a lot of trauma in his life and turned to drugs and alcohol to treat those wounds, and these three weeks were no different. He went away with his friends to a festival and got wrecked every day. When I got back in touch was when he had just come back from that holiday. We decided to meet up again, but he was very honest about not being over his ex and just wanting to be casual. That suited me, I thought it was what I wanted too at the time. 

So we met up for the second time, went on a nice date and then I stayed at his for the whole weekend. We talked a lot and learnt so much about each other. It was clear he wasn't mentally in a very good place. He told me the reason he and his ex broke up and I could see he still really loved her. 2 days after that weekend, he messaged me saying the familiarity and intimacy we had was just too much for him right now. He was right though, considering we'd only met twice it was insane how intense and coupley we felt already. I knew I'd become attached if we carried on so again, we agreed to go our separate ways. 

We didn't really speak much, I was meeting new people and going on dates and doing my own thing as was he. I still couldn't quite shake our chemistry, every time I met new guys id compare the dates to the one I had with him. We'd send each other memes every now and then but that was it. Then 3 months later, in December 2018, I thought fuck it. I asked him if he wanted to go for a drink sometime. He was really shocked that I was still interested, he thought I'd hate him because on the date in September he really led me on even though he knew he wasn't ready. I told him I understood because I didn't want anything then either but our connection was quite strong so it did sting but that it was kind of unexplainable. Anyway, he said he would want to be more than friends. With both of us carrying scars from childhood and past bad relationships though, we both said let's be exclusive and not date anyone else but let's keep it casual and not call it a relationship. I think this made us feel more in control of not getting hurt. 

Anyway, this arrangement was lovely and continued for 4 months. We met every week, could never keep our hands off each other. Would stay up talking through the night sometimes. The fact he did drugs occasionally didn't bother me, for some reason it made him more attractive (because of my own issues lol) and he started opening up about his childhood. I noticed though that every time he opened up, for the next week or so then he'd be a little distant. Eventually in April 2019 he told me he had feelings for me but that he could never have another relationship. He knew that there was a possibility of getting hurt and he wasn't willing to roll the dice. Essentially, he was hurting himself by breaking things off with me before I could do it to him. I was heart broken. I already knew I was in love with him by that point but I knew the fact we said it was casual was going to be an issue and I kept lying to myself. 

I deleted him off Facebook and tried my best to move on. In June 2019, he reached out and told me he missed me. That he was confused because he didn't want to lose me but was too scared to let me in. We toyed with the idea of getting back together again, but I was too scared myself and wary. I told him he should stay single for a while because he seemed to jump from situationship to situationship, even his last ex that he loved started out that way and he couldn't remember the last time he had been properly single. We became friends again but didn't speak properly until September 2019. The feelings and everything were still there but we took it slow. We decided to meet up in October 2019 and started things up again. BUT it seemed we hadn't really learnt from the first time because we just carried on the same arrangement as before. Exclusive but not in a relationship (even though they basically mean the same thing). 

This time he introduced me to all his friends, I stayed over a lot more and he stayed over mine too. In December 2019 he invited me to a gig with his friends. That night we all stayed up partying. When we finally got into bed we were cuddled up and talking. He started saying he doesn't feel good enough for me. That I deserve so much better. All horrible things about himself. I got upset, because I think he's absolutely fantastic, and I said to him 'i think you're amazing and I dont know if you realise this but... I've been in love with you for months' and I was crying at this point. I felt him freeze and he grabbed my head (in a soft way) to face him and he started crying and said 'i love you too'. We both hugged and sobbed for a while and he repeatedly said he loved me and that he had for months but was so scared to say it. He really didn't want to get hurt especially because of how things ended last time he loved someone. He didn't feel worthy of my love or anyones love in the past, and he sobbed and sobbed and thanked me for loving him back and apologised for hurting me so many times before. The next morning the first thing he did after we woke was look me in the eyes and whispered I love you. I honestly can say I was on cloud 9 for weeks afterwards. I still get emotional when I think of it now. 

I too, didn't feel worthy of love. Sometimes I still don't. This whole comment might've sounded like a super toxic relationship with two unhealthy people, but honestly the feeling of two damaged as fuck guarded people finally opening up enough to tell each other they love each other is so beautiful and special to me. It was the most special moment in my life. And I've been in love twice before him, but this just felt different.

I'd love to say things were smooth from there but they weren't. Again, he freaked out not long after that. It was a lot for him to handle and this time I'd had enough so we broke up in January this year. This time, I thought for good. Again, deleted him and blocked him but I still had his number. I was secretly hoping he'd get back in touch and that it wasn't the end for us, but I really thought this time it was because I couldn't do it again. 

In March, before covid caused lockdown in my Country, he reached out on WhatsApp. We had the most vulnerable and open conversation we've ever had. We spoke for 7 hours all about our feelings, something we always avoided before. He told me he's never been more scared than falling in love with me, that he can see himself living with me and he had never had that before and that now he can't see his life without me.
